sources.README.md:
# Draft workspace

The workspace lets a user open documents, edit their text, and move between
documents. It renders the active document together with an outline, a save badge,
and breadcrumb history. Saved document data remains available after navigation,
and workspace integrations may react to successful saves.

`select(id)`, `edit(text)`, and `close()` are the public navigation and editing
operations. The outline and breadcrumbs should continue to describe what the user
is viewing, while the store should retain accepted edits. Existing integrations
and ordinary navigation behavior must keep working when draft writes are
coalesced.

The shared trailing-task utility is also used by search preview. Preview is a
transient feature with its own hide behavior and is outside the requested draft
save change.

This fixture uses normal JavaScript modules and an injected timer adapter. No
framework lifecycle is simulated.

public_inputs.task:
# Coalesce draft saves in the workspace

The editor currently writes to the workspace store on every edit. Change editor
autosave to coalesce a burst of input: after 120 ms without another edit, save
only its latest text. Reuse the existing trailing-task utility where appropriate.
Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior. Keep
search preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task.

limitations: Departure flushing is a preservation deduction from the original immediate writes and fresh store reads, not an explicit universal before-return deadline.
Attempt 1 reports successful syntax checks and acceptance but supplies no behavioral observations. This establishes neither causality nor exhaustive correctness or cross-task benefit.
Public evidence establishes synchronous reentry through store notifications. It does not establish callbacks from renderers, timer operations, or subscription cleanup.
Exception recovery, timer cancellation races, mutable non-string inputs, and ordering of independent actions at identical deadlines are unspecified.
The current public API establishes no submission, receipt archive, persistent buffer bank, or framework lifecycle requirement.
This revision narrows applicability to the current public sources; it does not disprove ownership or submission rules supported by the related experiences' original tasks.

rules.body: Apply when coalescing editor persistence must preserve navigation, accepted edits, and a separate navigation projection while save integrations can synchronously navigate. TASK states: "autosave to coalesce a burst of input: after 120 ms without another edit, save\nonly its latest text. Reuse the existing trailing-task utility where appropriate." src/workspace.js states: "// Store notifications synchronously call integrations. Editor state and outline\n// projection are separate responsibilities; only this workspace connects them."

Enqueue the latest accepted text using the existing trailing-task utility with a 120 ms quiet interval, binding delayed work to the accepting document rather than consulting a later selection. Preserve empty text, subsequent bursts, and editing without a selection as a no-op. The original src/editor.js contains "if (current) store.write(current.id, text);"; src/trailing-task.js retains arguments with "pending = args;". These sources do not require an additional in-memory text model or persistent buffer bank.

After callback-capable departure saving, revalidate the open request before installing its destination and revalidate enclosing workspace navigation before committing or clearing its projection. Protect clearing effects as well as installation. src/draft-store.js directly invokes subscribers with "if (listeners.has(listener)) listener(event);"; src/workspace.js registers "const stop = store.subscribe(event => onSaved(event, navigation));". README.md requires: "The outline and breadcrumbs should continue to describe what the user\nis viewing, while the store should retain accepted edits." src/navigation-projection.js states: "// decides whether a requested visit was retained before committing it here." A superseded continuation must not publish a visit that the editor did not retain.

Preserve synchronous public interfaces, distinct visits, renderer payloads, event/revision semantics, listener snapshot and membership behavior, document-specific status filtering, captured subscription cleanup, and copied breadcrumb publication. src/workspace.js allocates "const visit = ++nextVisit;". src/save-status.js filters with "if (event.id === id) renderStatus(event);". src/navigation-projection.js contains "commit(visit) { selected = { ...visit }; trail.push({ ...visit }); publish(); }," and "clear() { selected = null; publish(); }," so clearing selection retains committed history. Preserve disposal's integration detachment before editor closure: src/workspace.js contains "dispose() { stop(); editor.close(); projection.clear(); }".

Determine departure scheduling from the current task and original behavior, rather than persistent ownership alone. Do not require persistent buffer reuse, caller-text copying, submission handling, or framework teardown without applicable public evidence. Keep transient preview policy separate: TASK states "search preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task." Preserve src/search-preview.js: "const task = createTrailingTask(query => publish({ query }), 40, timers);" and "hide() { task.cancel(); },". Do not transfer durable departure flushing to a feature whose explicit policy discards pending work.

Verify timer resetting, no active-burst write before 120 ms of quiet, one latest-text write per burst, later successful bursts, empty text, and no-selection editing. With pending text, exercise switch, same-document reopen, close, and dispose; check original-document persistence, fresh reads, and badge retirement. Trigger select and close through timer-driven and departure-driven store notifications, then edit the resulting visit; check that final selection, document output, projection, and breadcrumbs agree and that successor edits save independently without duplicate consumption. Check copied projection payloads and retained history on clear. Confirm preview's unchanged 40 ms delay, hide cancellation, and subsequent-query usability. These checks operationalize TASK's "Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior." and the cited public source semantics; they are not observations supplied by the acceptance verdict.

checkpoints: Several edits less than 120 ms apart produce no early write and one write containing the latest text after 120 ms of quiet.
A later editing burst saves successfully; empty text is accepted and editing without a selection does nothing.
Switching documents, reopening the same document, closing, and disposing preserve the departing document's pending accepted text before returning.
Reopening a document reads its newly persisted text.
Inline save integrations that select or close leave editor selection, document output, outline, and breadcrumbs consistent with the retained navigation.
Edits accepted during a save notification form independent pending work and are neither duplicated nor erased by completion of the earlier save.
A departing badge emits no output during departure flushing; active badges retain document filtering.
Search preview retains its 40 ms delay, cancellation on hide, and usability for subsequent queries.
forbidden_effects: Writing every edit immediately during an uninterrupted editing burst.
Saving pending text under a document selected after the edit was accepted.
Discarding accepted document edits merely because their editor visit closes.
Allowing an outer navigation continuation to overwrite or clear a visit retained by navigation invoked synchronously during its departure save.
Publishing a projection or breadcrumb entry for an open request that did not retain its editor visit.
Emitting a departing badge's status during navigation.
Clearing callback-enqueued pending work after an earlier batch finishes.
Changing search preview timing or hide cancellation.
lifecycle_identity: Pending edits retain the identity of the document that accepted them, independently of the later selection.
Each workspace select allocates a distinct visit, including selection of the same document id.
The mounted visit owns its save-status subscription; retiring that subscription does not discard accepted document persistence.
Editor selection and committed projection must refer to the same retained visit.
The contract does not require a persistent buffer bank or any particular internal ownership structure.

Retire consumed pending state before calling store.write.
Detach the departing badge before flushing its pending write.

Revalidate navigation authority after callback-capable editor departure and before installing a destination or publishing projection changes.

Store writes update records before inline notification, increment revision once per actual write, and preserve listener snapshot and membership semantics.

rules.body:
Apply when deferred editor persistence must preserve synchronous departure persistence, inline save-listener navigation, and entry-bound submissions with visit-bound notices. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet
interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts
must continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." README.md states: "When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is readable
from the store. A close/open request retires its previous save badge immediately."

Update the accepting editor's in-memory text synchronously, then enqueue persistence using the existing trailing-task utility with a 120 ms quiet interval. Bind delayed work to the accepting document rather than consulting the later selection. Preserve editing without a selection as a no-op and allow empty text. src/editor.js contains "if (!current) return;" and "current.text = text;". TASK requires: "Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." The internal ownership structure may vary if these observable requirements hold.

On departure, capture the old editor resources, revoke current ownership, detach its badge, and complete old-view clearing before flushing its pending persistence, or protect any remaining effects against newer navigation. Flush before reading a replacement document. Recheck navigation request authority after callback-capable persistence before installing a destination. README.md states: "Reopening a document restores its saved text in a new editor visit." It also states: "Navigation precedence is
ordered by request start: a request that starts later wins even when an earlier
request returns afterward." src/save-status.js requires that the departing badge "must produce no further output, including during that
// navigation call." Cleanup must use captured departing resources so it cannot detach or erase a successor's resources or edits.

At submission entry, capture the originating visit and its document/text snapshot before persistence can invoke integrations. Persist the accepted text before archive capture, then create and return exactly one receipt even if persistence navigates or accepts further edits. README.md states: "`submit()` accepts the document and latest text selected at its call entry." It further requires: "Accepted text\nmust be persisted before the archive captures the receipt. Later edits or\nnavigation cannot change that receipt's document, text, or obligation to exist." Preserve the no-selection null result without creating a receipt.

Authorize submission notice output using the exact originating visit after callback-capable persistence; receipt validity and notice permission have separate lifetimes. README.md states: "Its visible submission notice belongs only
to the editor visit that accepted the action: it may appear only if that same
visit is still active when the notice is emitted." It also states: "Reopening the same document
creates a different visit. Any navigation clears the previous submission notice." An uninterrupted submit must display its receipt and leave editing usable. Do not use document-ID equality to represent visit identity or infer authority from receipt contents.

Preserve synchronous workspace interfaces, store event/revision semantics, live status filtering, subscription cleanup, renderer argument shapes, and immutable archive snapshots with copied listings. src/save-status.js filters with "if (event.id === id) renderStatus(event);" src/receipt-archive.js contains "const receipt = Object.freeze({ id, text });" and "list() { return receipts.map(receipt => ({ ...receipt })); }," Preserve disposal ordering from src/workspace.js: "return { ...navigation, dispose() { stop(); navigation.close(); } };" Keep preview behavior separate: TASK states "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/search-preview.js uses "const task = createTrailingTask(query => publish({ query }), 40, timers);" and "hide() { task.cancel(); },".

Do not generalize departure flushing to contracts that explicitly discard pending work, require persistent buffer banks merely because documents persist, or introduce callbacks from output sinks. README.md states: "Render functions and the receipt archive are output\nsinks and never call back into the workspace." A final installation guard alone does not protect stale clearing effects after store callbacks; complete those effects first or validate their authority.

Check timer resetting, no write before 120 ms of quiet, one latest-text write per burst, later successful bursts, empty text, and no-selection editing. With pending edits, exercise switch, same-document reopen, close, and dispose; verify before-return persistence, fresh reads, and immediate badge retirement. Trigger nested open or close from timer-, departure-, and submission-driven store notifications, and edit the resulting visit; verify later navigation wins, successor output survives, and callback-enqueued work saves independently without duplicate consumption. During submit, independently verify the entry snapshot, persistence before capture, exactly one returned receipt, notice suppression after navigation or same-document reopening, uninterrupted notice output, and subsequent editing. Check no-selection submission and unchanged preview delay, hide cancellation, and later-query usability. These checks derive from TASK and public source obligations, not from the acceptance verdict.

notes: Training-only; not approved for long-term retrieval.

limitations: The supplied source does not expose integration detachment facilities. README.md states "Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace." Preserve that ordering where those facilities exist; do not invent an adapter API.

Timer exception behavior and cancellation races are unspecified. The supplied Store.stop deletes a subscription without invoking application callbacks; callback-capable cleanup is not established here.
Attempt 1 passed the reported checks, but no behavioral observations were supplied. This does not establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or cross-task effectiveness.
Unreviewed provisional training guidance; effectiveness unknown.

rules.body: Apply when introducing trailing persistence into a synchronous editor whose save listeners can navigate. TASK requires "after a 120 ms quiet interval write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts must continue to save." README.md requires "Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text." These requirements make persistence boundaries and visit identity part of preserving supported behavior.

Keep the visit's immutable in-memory text current immediately, then push it into that visit's reusable trailing task. Preserve pending edits at departure and before submission capture rather than canceling them. Preserve the utility's clearing of pending state before invoking work: src/workflow.rb contains "    @handle = @pending = nil\n    @work.call(value) unless value.nil?" This allows edits admitted by a save callback to form an independent subsequent batch.

Capture the departing visit and remove its current ownership before flushing its pending save. Finish its passive clearing output before the flush, or guard remaining output after callbacks. Complete cleanup using the captured visit. After departure, an outer open must recheck its navigation request before installing its destination. Saving is callback-capable: src/workflow.rb states "    @listeners.to_a.each { |token, block| block.call(event) if @listeners.key?(token) }" Nested navigation, edits, subscriptions and rendering must remain authoritative.

For submission, capture the selected visit, its snapshot and its confirmation capability before flushing pending persistence. Flush before archive capture, then return the receipt even if navigation suppresses its notice. Recheck the originating visit immediately before notice output, including after archive listeners run. README.md states "An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity." src/workflow.rb enforces identity with "  def active;!@owner.nil?&&@owner.equal?(@current.call);end".

Preserve synchronous public interfaces, immutable text copies, subscription delivery and fresh visits, including reopening the same document ID. Preserve the null result when no editor is selected and receipt delivery independently of notice permission. Leave preview scheduling and cancellation unchanged: TASK states "Preserve other supported behavior and the synchronous public interfaces. The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change."

Do not let a successful receipt authorize output for a retired visit, use document ID equality as visit identity, or assume that code after a save still owns navigation. A guard on final installation alone does not protect stale clearing output. Apply the current task's explicit boundary policy; this guidance does not require flushing work that another contract explicitly discards.

Check several edits within 120 ms yield one latest-text write and a later burst saves again. Check close, switch, same-document reopening and disposal preserve pending text. During timer-driven, departure-driven and submission-driven saves, have a store listener open or close the workspace and edit the resulting visit; verify the outer continuation preserves that visit and its pending batch. During submission, navigate from both store and archive listeners; verify the original snapshot and returned receipt survive while stale notices are suppressed. Also check no-selection submission, subscription delivery, and the unchanged 40 ms preview and hide behavior.

candidate_sources.README.md:
# Draft workspace

The workspace lets a user open documents, edit their text, and move between
documents. It renders the active document together with an outline, a save badge,
and breadcrumb history. Saved document data remains available after navigation,
and workspace integrations may react to successful saves.

`select(id)`, `edit(text)`, and `close()` are the public navigation and editing
operations. The outline and breadcrumbs should continue to describe what the user
is viewing, while the store should retain accepted edits. Existing integrations
and ordinary navigation behavior must keep working when draft writes are
coalesced.

The shared trailing-task utility is also used by search preview. Preview is a
transient feature with its own hide behavior and is outside the requested draft
save change.

This fixture uses normal JavaScript modules and an injected timer adapter. No
framework lifecycle is simulated.
